dedupe_keys.name: occdem statistically based occupancy and occupant driven electrical and hot water demand profiles

description: OccDem is a program that generates statistically based occupancy profiles and the electrical and hot water demand that follows from occupant activity, for one household or many. It was written by Graeme Flett at the University of Strathclyde and published on the university's research portal on 2 March 2021, replacing an earlier version (OccDem_0d, doi 10.15129/ef54ba37-354a-40b6-9ec0-8d21cce92263) released in 2019; the portal gives October 2013 to March 2020 as the period of data production. The input is information on the population being modelled; outputs are occupancy and occupancy-driven electrical and hot water demand profiles. Coverage: generic households defined by the user; the statistics behind the profiles are not described on the pages read, and it was developed at a UK university. Access: a 76 MB zip from the Strathclyde portal, run through the OccDem_0.2 executable. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: the program is written in Python but ships as a Windows 10 executable; other versions are available on request from the creator. Simulation uses: building performance simulation, stock modelling, district heating analysis, energy flexibility and smart grid studies, as the description lists. Related records: the Bolzano multi-family monitoring dataset and the Vienna office occupant dataset.
inputs: Information on the population of people being modelled
